text: Remove wrapped-agent permission-bypass launch flags and enforce least-authority process arguments
description: Remove explicit --dangerously-skip-permissions launch arguments from Claude, Agy, and Grok worker and watchdog profiles. Add a fail-closed common process-argument policy at the actual worker/watchdog spawn boundary that rejects known permission/sandbox bypass flags, with focused tests. Preserve resume/model behavior, do not add replacement grants, and do not launch, stop, or restart sessions.

reflections.context: A production capability audit found that Claude, Agy, and Grok worker and watchdog profiles always supplied --dangerously-skip-permissions. That execution-level capability bypass sat beneath the newly enforced supervisor dispatch authority boundary.
reflections.outcome: Removed the bypass flag from all six affected process argument builders while preserving resume and model selection. Added a shared fail-closed process argument policy at the actual spawn boundary for worker and watchdog roles, covering known standalone, split, and equals-form approval bypasses. Validation occurs before replacing a worker and both initial role argument sets are checked before any process is spawned.
reflections.effectiveness: The complete wrapped-agents/common suite passes 167/167 tests, including four new policy tests. Common, Claude session, Agy session, and Grok session TypeScript checks all pass; git diff --check passes. A source audit finds bypass spellings only in the enforcing policy and negative tests. No server or session was launched, stopped, restarted, or replaced.
reflections.lesson: A policy on supervisor-generated terminal actions is insufficient if the underlying CLI starts with blanket approval bypasses. Capability constraints must be checked again at the irreversible process-creation boundary, before disturbing an existing process.
reflections.pattern: Enforce least authority twice: remove unsafe defaults from profiles, then reject permission-bypass arguments centrally at the last pre-spawn boundary.

supportingConnections.explanation: Extends least authority from process capabilities to the network control surface.

status.comment: Least-authority launch profiles and fail-closed pre-spawn policy implemented and internally verified; awaiting explicit user acceptance before done.

valueRationale: An explicit permission bypass lets autonomous workers act outside the human authorization boundary, so removing and mechanically prohibiting it is a prerequisite for safe capability growth.
